runs.name: Magnitude International Ltd; Nasdaq MAGH (halted), SEC CIK 0002046117, Cayman Islands, Form 20-F, fiscal year to April 30, IFRS in Singapore dollars; electrical works subcontractor in Singapore, mainly residential and mixed developments; 1:40 forward split and reorganization 2025-05-27, IPO August 2025, SEC trading suspension December 2025, Nasdaq delisting determination 2026-08-03 under appeal
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **US$6.76** (last trade 2025-12-04, aggregator, flagged; untradeable: SEC suspension 2025-12-05 to 2025-12-18, Nasdaq halt from 2025-12-19, delisting determination 2026-08-03 under IM-5101-4, appealed). Shares **35,000,000**, one class (20-F FY2026 cover, `0001493152-26-043050`, checked as 33,350,000 before the IPO plus 1,650,000 sold); cap US$236.6M, S$301.4M at the filer's convenience rate. Sovereign **2.62%** (SGD: the 50-year Singapore Government Securities benchmark NC22300W, Monetary Authority of Singapore, close of 2026-10-16; the protocol's table has no SGD row). Filings read: 20-F FY2026 (`0001493152-26-043050`, filed late after NT 20-F `0001493152-26-040731`), 20-F FY2025 (`0001493152-25-013424`) and its 20-F/A (`0001493152-26-008628`, at the SEC's request, CORRESP of 2026-03-03 and 2026-03-06), the 424B4 of 2025-08-12 (`0001641172-25-023166`, FY2023 and FY2024), five 6-Ks. Cross-check: FY2024 revenue S$24,201,834 and net profit S$2,007,469 agree in the 424B4 and the 2026 20-F. `tools/run.py` returned nothing for this IFRS 20-F filer; every figure by hand. Four audited years only (private until 2025). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 4, 3.D and 5 (six, listed in the run file). Rivals: the 20-F names none ("large international players mainly from China and India", unnamed); FBS Global (FBGL) and SKK Holdings (SKK) read as a CONVENTION of the run. **Q1 IN** (Singapore electrical subcontractor on residential and mixed developments, revenue S$21.9M, 24.2M, 15.4M, 19.1M FY2023 to FY2026, backlog S$85.0M). **Q2 OUT** **[L2004-003]**, **[M2017-009]**, **[M2012-109]**, **[M1997-010]**, **[L2007-004]**, **[M2011-015]**: all revenue from competitive tenders, not recurring; cost-plus pricing with the mark-up cut to win; over 2,200 contractors on the same BCA workhead, about 240 at Grade L5 or above; top five customers 77% to 88%; an onerous-contract provision of S$1.97M at 2022-05-01; gross margin 12.1%, 15.9%, 15.5%, 10.5%; no cost advantage claimed; operating margins 3.6%, 8.4%, 0.5%, -11.6% against FBS Global -0.2%, -7.0%, -7.5% and SKK 3.4%, 4.6%, -19.6%. After the stop, integrity facts recorded, not judged: US$1.4M of IPO money lent unsecured at 8% to two unnamed third parties from the closing date, not a stated use, Item 14 reading "None."; S$1.6M of dividends declared to the CEO in FY2025 against profit of S$42,980, S$600,000 unpaid; five entities subscribed 23.7% for about US$9K each before the IPO; the price from US$1.37 to US$6.76 in three weeks before the suspension (the company denies any connection); late and amended filings; bank debt on the CEO's personal guarantee. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash (all-equity, from the filed cash-flow statements) S$893,701, S$546,530, (S$978,100), (S$1,989,108), average **(S$381,744)**; the series changes sign, so the range is the no-growth case alone, **(S$0.44), (US$0.35) a share**; S$0.046 with the FY2026 fees the filer calls one-time added back; a ceiling outside the convention (a CONVENTION of the run) US$1.43; fair price **negative, (US$0.11) a share all-equity and equity-only**; no case earns the floor; not armed. Contamination declared by the analyst: MAGN commit subjects with its box, a date-filtered `Test Runs/` listing showing other companies' run file names (no MAGH file), AYI and ARCB research-folder names, memory index lines; none used. Commits a8e969b5 (template), 624eab22 (Step 0, foundations, standing rule, Q1), dcba990d (Q2 to the end, committed by the dispatcher: the analyst met an `.git/index.lock` of 11:27 it could not wait out and did not delete it). Position note filled at the fold. Citations: the analyst's `check_run.py` 33 ids, 22 fragments, no problem; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_check.py`, 22 fragments closing before an id, none outside its row; no E-ids; **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **Dispatcher's error, recorded:** the brief called the company a British Virgin Islands holding company (read from EDGAR's state code); the 20-F says the Cayman Islands, the BVI company being the intermediate Elec Power Ltd; the analyst caught it. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) a four-year window from a company private until 2025, window or TOO HARD (WORK) on the base; (2) specific (b) on a sign-changing series leaves a single negative case and a negative fair price, reporting unstated; (3) Step 0's eight to ten balance sheets when four exist; (4) no SGD row in the sovereign table; (5) Q2's commodity paragraph written for a commodity price, not a commodity service sold by tender; (6) a halted, untradeable last quote as the price for the floor test. Could not get: years before FY2023 beyond the 2022 provision; any named rival; a live price.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 (Magnitude International, Nasdaq MAGH, halted since December 2025 and facing delisting; a Singapore electrical subcontractor that wins every contract by competitive tender at cost plus a mark-up it cuts to win, among over 2,200 registered contractors, top five customers 77% to 88%, no cost advantage claimed, gross margin 10.5% to 15.9%, and a field whose SEC filers earn a few percent or lose money. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: IPO money lent unsecured to unnamed third parties, pre-IPO dividends to the CEO far above profit, cheap pre-IPO allotments, a fourfold rise before the SEC suspension, late and amended filings. Computation beneath the stop: owner cash negative on average, value (US$0.35) a share against a last trade of US$6.76, fair price negative, not armed. No citation slip; the brief's BVI line was the dispatcher's error. Framework gaps for the operator: a four-year window, a negative single case, short balance-sheet history, no SGD sovereign row, a commodity service sold by tender, an untradeable price.)
